calls.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kadri sparks a Avalanche comeback
paras: The first period was a wild one. Wyatt Kaiser got the scoring started for the Blackhawks just 57 seconds into the game. Roman Kantserov made it 2-0 early in the first, but they didn’t score again. Colorado had a goal taken off for goalie interference midway through the period, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scored 26 seconds apart late in the period to tie it 2-2. Kadri scored his second of the night on the power play midway through the second to put the Avalanche ahead and complete the comeback. The Blackhawks’ Patrick Kane left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was ruled out with an upper-body injury. Schwartz scored his second of the night with 11 seconds left in the period to make it 4-2 for the Avalanche. Devon Toews added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 5-2.

The Avalanche had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Blackhawks 29-23. The Blackhawks hit two posts and the crossbar and still lost. Mackenzie Blackwood settled in after a shaky start for the Avalanche: he gave up two goals on the first three shots, then stopped the last 20, and Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Sam Malinski had the best night of anyone.
The Avalanche killed all four Blackhawks power plays. The Avs improved to 9-5-1 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Blackhawks fell to 4-10-1, still last in the Central.
